summary.prose: Building this Story replaces the fixed 30-minute wait on a daemon code review with an idle limit that every progress frame restarts, inside a configurable overall ceiling. The code-review runner reports each review call as progress; the step.call host gains a way to forward a step tool's progress, and the code-review step relays the daemon's frames through it, so the MCP client sees a live tool instead of a silent one. The work ends by shipping to the installed daemon and rerunning the blocked code review of Epic 86197ac6 Story s2.

tasks.title: Idle limit in the shared review stream wait
tasks.summary: Add optional idleMs to ReviewStreamOpts (src/shared/review-stream.ts). runReviewStream arms an idle timer alongside the overall timeoutMs timer; every progress/delta frame restarts the idle timer only. On expiry fail with ReviewStreamError('timeout') whose message names which limit ran out, and cancel the transport as today. Without idleMs (or with an idleMs not > 0 or not below timeoutMs), behaviour is unchanged.
acceptanceChecks: Frames arriving more often than idleMs keep a request alive past idleMs; it resolves on its final frame
No frame for idleMs fails 'timeout' with a message naming the idle limit and cancels the transport
Frames never extend timeoutMs; past it the request fails 'timeout' naming the ceiling
A caller passing no idleMs gets today's single wait (existing review-stream tests pass unchanged)
An idleMs that is not > 0 or not below timeoutMs arms no idle timer: the single wait applies

tasks.title: Per-call progress from the code-review runner
tasks.summary: Add optional onCall to JudgeContext (src/workflow/code-review/types.ts); runDimensionJob (src/workflow/review-pipeline/code-review.ts) forwards ctx.onCall as runReviewJob's existing onCall. Add phase 'call' to CodeReviewProgress (src/workflow/code-review/runner.ts); runCodeReview builds a per-dimension onCall that emits { phase: 'call', dimension, detail: '<stage> <role> #n' }.

tasks.title: Progress frames from step tools on step.call
tasks.summary: Extend StepToolRunner (src/daemon/steps/host.ts) with an optional third progress argument. createStepCallHandler passes a progress callback that sends each call as a 'progress' frame on the step.call stream before 'done'; a send that throws or hits a closed stream is swallowed and logged at debug; progress after the final frame is ignored. Other step tools are untouched. The MCP forwarder (src/mcp/server.ts) is consumed unchanged; a regression test proves it relays these frames.
acceptanceChecks: A step tool's progress calls arrive as 'progress' frames before the 'done' frame
A failing progress send does not fail the step; it still answers with its envelope
A progress call after the final frame is ignored
Regression test, no change to src/mcp/server.ts: the existing forwarder relays step.call progress frames as notifications/progress when the client sent a progressToken

tests.name: step.call: a step tool's progress calls arrive as 'progress' frames before 'done'; a failing send does not fail the step; progress after 'done' is ignored
MCP forwarder: a forwarded insrc_code_review_step with a progressToken emits notifications/progress for each progress frame

tasks.title: Configurable code-review wait limits and progress relay in the step
tasks.summary: Declare codeReview.daemonReviewCeilingMs (14_400_000) and codeReview.daemonReviewIdleMs (1_200_000) in src/config/config-catalog.ts and bump the catalog-contract row count (43 -> 45). Replace DAEMON_CODE_REVIEW_WAIT_MS in src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts with codeReviewWaitLimits(), read fail-safe like readFreshnessTimeoutMs with idle clamped to the ceiling. reviewByDaemon passes timeoutMs/idleMs and an onFrame that relays every frame to the new CodeReviewStepDeps.progress; a timeout answers with the cause and names the config key to raise. host.ts:69 threads the runner's progress into the deps. routing.test.ts asserts codeReviewWaitLimits' defaults instead of the removed constant.

tasks.title: End-to-end proof: a review longer than 30 minutes completes
tasks.summary: Integration test with a stubbed model and fake clock driving the code-review step through the in-daemon client: a review reporting a call every minute runs past 30 minutes and completes, writing its record; one that goes quiet past the idle limit fails with the idle cause and writes no record (never falling back to a controller review).

A daemon code review that goes silent past idleMs fails next:'error' with the idle cause and writes no record
